guide.title: Bolton Valley Resort, Vermont: the DesLauriers family's mountain, bought back in 2017
guide.intro: Bolton Valley was founded in 1966 by Ralph DesLauriers and his father, per Wikipedia's Bolton Valley Resort article, and remains family-owned and operated today, run by four of Ralph DesLauriers' children: Lindsay, Evan, Adam, and Eric, according to the resort's own About Us page. Beginning around 1997 the resort passed through a series of outside owners and struggled financially; in spring 2017 Ralph DesLauriers and a small group of investors purchased the mountain back, returning it to local ownership.

sections.heading: Lifts and lodging through the decades
sections.body: Chateau des Monts, a 20-unit hotel condominium complex, was completed at the resort in 1971, per Wikipedia. The Vista Quad chairlift, installed in 2005, serves as the main lift out of the base area; the Wilderness Double, dating to 1966, is the longest lift on the mountain. The resort offers night skiing and riding on a portion of its trails, typically five nights a week from 4 to 10pm, according to Bolton Valley's own Night Skiing page. Bolton Valley's own site states it offers 71 trails across 300 skiable acres.

sections.heading: Energy, awards, and riders
sections.body: In 2009 Bolton Valley installed a Northwind 100 wind turbine, per Wikipedia's Bolton Valley Resort article. In 2010 Bolton Valley received the National Ski Areas Association's Silver Eagle Award for Energy Conservation/Clean Energy, according to the resort's own About Us page. Professional snowboarder Jake Blauvelt grew up at Bolton Valley and hosts an annual banked slalom event there, per Wikipedia.

faq.question: Is Bolton Valley still owned by the DesLauriers family?
faq.answer: Yes. Ralph DesLauriers and his father founded the resort in 1966. After a stretch of outside ownership beginning around 1997, Ralph DesLauriers and a small group of investors bought the mountain back in spring 2017, and it is run today by four of his children, per the resort's own About Us page.

faq.question: Does Bolton Valley offer night skiing?
faq.answer: Yes. The resort offers night skiing and riding on a portion of its trails, typically five nights a week from 4 to 10pm, according to Bolton Valley's own Night Skiing page.
